text:
incident-bot: [ALERT] Elevated 5xx and inference errors for model 'omega' variant 'v2-quant' in eu-west-1. 5xx rate 4.8% over last 5m, baseline ~0.1%. Tail latency spikes >2s. Auto-slo-fallback not triggered yet.

maya (oncall): seeing the alert. paging now. I'm taking incident.

joseph: thx. quick readout — we're seeing a pattern of decoding failures after 256 tokens for this variant only. Logs show repeated 'kv-cache mismatch' errors.

liam (sre): confirmed from runtime traces — gpu worker nodes hitting CUDA memcopy timeout during kv cache restore. Looks correlated with the quantized kernel path.

maya (oncall): immediate mitigation proposals: 1) remove v2-quant from routing (route to omega-stable), 2) apply emergency quota to heavy keys, 3) notify impacted customers. Which one do we want first?

joseph: do #1 now. We'll be able to roll traffic to omega-stable (same model but non-quant) — latency will increase slightly but should be reliable. I can run the disable command.

maya (oncall): go ahead, run it and paste the command so I can approve.

joseph: running rwctl to disable variant.

joseph: ```bash
# disable routing for a variant (no infra change, router config only)
rwctl variant disable --model omega --variant v2-quant --region eu-west-1 --reason "high-5xx kv-cache timeout"
```

deploy-bot: INFO: Initiating routing change: remove variant omega:v2-quant from weighted routing table in eu-west-1 (initiated by joseph). Request id: r-0a1b2c3d

ops-bot: Routing update applied: omega:v2-quant removed from weights; omega:stable bumped to absorb traffic. New weights: stable=1.00.

maya (oncall): monitoring metrics now. please keep alerts quieted for noisy spikes. I'll open an incident page.

incident-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0456. PagerDuty alert acknowledged by maya.

alan (support): quick Q — any known customers impacted? I can start proactive outreach if we need to.

joseph: early sampling from logs shows a handful of high-volume API keys getting errors: key: cust-ams-42 (SaaS app), cust-retail-7, and many internal CI keys. Not yet prod-critical for revenue but we should treat as P1 for user-facing apps.

liam (sre): tail latencies dropped back to baseline after routing change. 5xx rate down to 0.2% in 2m. Good.

maya (oncall): great. next steps: 1) enforce emergency per-key quotas for heavy clients to prevent flapping while we investigate, 2) gather a dump from affected workers, 3) decide whether to rollback quant variant globally or just keep it shelved.

joseph: I'll push per-key quota using quota-manager. Command: ```bash
quota-manager set --key cust-ams-42 --qps 2 --reason "emergency-mitigate" && quota-manager set --key cust-retail-7 --qps 1
```

ops-bot: Quotas applied for cust-ams-42 and cust-retail-7.

alan (support): I'll draft a short message for the top 3 affected customers: what to include?

maya (oncall): include that we detected transient inference errors for a specific quantized model variant, that we have routed traffic to a stable variant, that you may see slightly higher latency, and we're monitoring; give an ETA for a root-cause update in 2 hours.

alan (support): posting messages now.

alan (support): @cust-ams-42 (via support) — we proactively rerouted traffic to a stable variant; you might see latency increase ~200ms; no data loss. Follow-up will be posted to your case in 2h.

joseph: collecting debug artifacts: core dumps, runtime logs, kernel traces. Start remote collection: 

joseph: ```bash
# fetch logs from nodes in eu-west-1 with tag omega-v2-quant
node-ctl fetch-logs --tag "omega:v2-quant" --since 10m --out /tmp/omega-quant-logs.tar.gz
```

liam (sre): I'm seeing multiple nodes with nvme I/O spikes then memcopy timeouts — possible driver regression in the quantized kernel path. Let's pin the hypothesis: quant kernel optimized memcpy introduced race under heavy KV restore.

maya (oncall): good hypothesis. joseph, can we repro in staging with same quant kernel?\
joseph: starting a staging replay now with sampled request traces. If repro, we'll hotpatch or roll the quant kernel back.

deploy-bot: Rollout blocker: cannot hotpatch kernel-level ops in prod without a canary. Recommend keeping variant disabled and schedule a controlled rollback of the quant kernel build.

maya (oncall): agree — keep variant disabled. We'll create an emergency release to roll back the quant kernels on affected nodes only if staging repros.

liam (sre): We should also update the routing guard to automatically prevent re-enabling v2-quant via automation until we've cleared a health check. I'll add a temporary circuit-breaker flag.

joseph: added feature flag: `circuit_breaker/omega/v2-quant/guarded=true`. Command: ```bash
feature-flag set circuit_breaker/omega/v2-quant/guarded true --expires 3h --note "block auto-reenable until RCA"
```

ops-bot: Feature flag set.

maya (oncall): handoff incoming — liam, joseph, I'm going offline for 30m to grab dinner; liam you'll take primary until I return.

liam (sre): taking over. I'll keep monitoring and coordinate with joseph on debug.

incident-bot: PagerDuty: handoff acknowledged — liam is now Primary on-call for INC-2026-0456.

liam (sre): status update 15m in: traffic fully shifted to omega:stable; 5xx down to 0.08%; tail latencies stable. Staging replay started by joseph; collecting failures.

joseph: repro succeeded in staging — kv-cache restore failing under concurrent restore load with quant kernel 0.9.2. We'll prepare a rollback to 0.9.1.

liam (sre): what's the blast radius for rolling kernel back to 0.9.1 on eu-west-1 inference fleet? Can we do a canary subset first?

joseph: yes — canary 10% nodes in eu-west-1 first. Plan: 1) deploy 0.9.1 to canary pool, 2) run health checks with live replay, 3) if green, roll remaining nodes.

deploy-bot: Canary deployment scheduled: kernel-rollout 0.9.1 -> canary (10% nodes) in eu-west-1. Initiated by joseph.

ops-bot: Canary deployed. Health check started.

liam (sre): monitoring canary. If canary green in 10m, proceed to full roll. If canary fails, we'll keep variant disabled and escalate to engineering-core.

joseph: canary passed basic checks. Running replay check now.

joseph: replay check OK, med-low error rate, KV restore stable. Proceeding to full rollout.

deploy-bot: Full rollout in progress: kernel 0.9.1 -> remaining nodes in eu-west-1.

ops-bot: Rollout completed. All inference workers report kernel 0.9.1.

liam (sre): metrics post-rollout: 5xx down to baseline 0.05%, tail latency back to normal.

maya (oncall): I'm back — thanks for the handoff. What's the plan for v2-quant? Keep disabled until we run an extended soak in staging and run a canary with lower concurrency?

joseph: yes. We'll add additional telemetry, run a long soak in staging, and build a new quant kernel with race fixes. Recommendation: keep v2-quant disabled for 48h and remove from auto-rollout.

alan (support): updating customer notes — sent the RCA to the top impacted customers and marked the issue resolved from their perspective; mention that performance returned to normal after routing and kernel rollback.

incident-bot: INC-2026-0456 — mitigation complete, monitoring. Postmortem templated — please add notes to the incident page.

maya (oncall): closing the thread here. Key takeaways: 1) disabled risky variant quickly, 2) applied per-key quotas to limit blast radius, 3) rolled kernel back via canary -> full rollout, 4) communicate to customers. Assign postmortem owner: joseph.

joseph: taking postmortem. I'll draft timeline + RCA + remediation steps (improve canary tests for quant kernels, add KV-restore watchdog, block auto-reenable for variants without health gating).

liam (sre): thanks everyone.

incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-0456 marked as RESOLVED by maya.

maya (oncall): closing. :white_check_mark:
